title: Spot-on-lawn (halo) assay for screening viruses in cultures and isolates
author: Kenneth M. Stedman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.eagbabw

steps.title: Preincubate Gelrite plates
steps.instruction: Place the Gelrite plates in a dry incubator at approximately 80 °C for about 10 minutes (00:10:00) to dry.

steps.title: Prepare softlayer
steps.instruction: Boil 10 mL of Sulfolobus medium containing roughly 0.2 % (w/v) Gelrite until the Gelrite fully dissolves, then allow the mixture to cool slightly to about 80 °C.

steps.title: Mix host cells with softlayer
steps.instruction: Add approximately 3 mL of the cooled softlayer to about 0.2 mL of exponentially growing Sulfolobus solfataricus cells, swirl to mix, and spread the mixture onto a pre‑incubated Gelrite plate; let the Gelrite solidify.

steps.title: Spot test samples
steps.instruction: After the Gelrite has solidified, spot 1–2 µL of each culture or supernatant to be screened onto the plate.

steps.title: Add positive control
steps.instruction: Spot 1 µL of a 0.01 % (v/v) Triton X‑100 solution onto the plate as a positive control.

steps.title: Incubate and examine plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at the same temperature used for growth for 2–3 days (72:00:00) and then examine for clearing zones around the spots.
